newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarussians, Russians try to ease Belarus crisis.
newsitem.headline: Belarussians, Russians try to ease Belarus crisis.

text.p: Semyon Sharetsky, the chairman of the Belarussian parliament, met two Russian parliamentary leaders on Russian soil on Wednesday to discuss the political crisis in Belarus.

Gennady Seleznyov and Yegor Stroyev, the chairmen of Russia's two chambers of parliament who are trying to mediate in the crisis, began talks with Sharetsky in the local parliament building in the western Russian city of Smolensk.

The talks in Smolensk, about 340 km (210 miles) west of Moscow, are intended to help defuse a crisis in which the parliament is opposing President Alexander Lukashenko's planned referendum on Sunday to increase his powers.
Lukashenko refused to attend the talks with Sharetsky, his main political opponent. An aide said the president had wanted Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to attend the meeting.
Lukashenko and Chernomyrdin were expected to meet on Friday or Saturday instead, a Lukashenko aide told Reuters. Moscow did not immediately confirm the report.
Officials with the two delegations in Smolensk said it was not clear if the parliamentary leaders would talk to reporters after the meeting. They gave no details of the discussions.
